records.name: Diagnostic accuracy
records.kind: Mathematical domain; no universal performance grades
records.range: 0–1 inclusive, or 0–100%; undefined when the required denominator is zero.
records.study: Histopathological examination/report of the removed appendix is the project’s operational reference standard for appendicitis disease status. Confirm this against the approved protocol; the original protocol document is not bundled. Original histology codes 1–5 are reference-positive; code 6 is reference-negative only when it represents isolated reactive lymphoid hyperplasia without appendicitis. Missing, unlisted or contradictory findings require review and are not automatically negative.
records.qualification: The reference-positive proportion weights Sensitivity; the reference-negative proportion weights Specificity. This is the analysed cohort’s disease proportion, not automatically population prevalence. In an operated-only or case-control sample it may differ from the intended clinical population. Accuracy generally requires those group proportions as well as Sensitivity and Specificity; do not combine estimates from different cohorts or thresholds. (Sensitivity + Specificity) / 2 is binary unadjusted balanced accuracy, not generally ordinary Accuracy. Ordinary Accuracy equals that mean when p = 0.5 or Sensitivity = Specificity. Balanced accuracy is not a new analysis or clinical-usefulness judgement in this app. Accuracy can conceal poor performance in the less common reference class and does not alone establish clinical usefulness. Taking the simple mean as ordinary Accuracy, substituting population prevalence for the analysed cohort proportion, or mixing cohorts, thresholds or rounded rates. Exact identity for one unweighted binary 2 × 2 table, the same eligible cohort, disease target, reference standard and index-test threshold, with N >0 and both reference classes present so Sensitivity and Specificity are defined. Use unrounded proportions (0–1), not a mixture of percentages and proportions. Changing the disease proportion changes the weight given to each reference class. Holding Sensitivity and Specificity fixed illustrates this dependence, but their values can also change between clinical settings. If one reference class is absent, one class-specific rate is undefined: do not multiply an undefined rate by zero; overall Accuracy can still be calculated directly when N >0.
